name: 序列帧动画
description: 制作连续动作序列帧，切帧并合成 GIF 动画。
instructions:
## Purpose
Create short sprite animations with continuous motion, not a collection of unrelated poses. Reply in the user's language.

## Inputs
Reuse this session's character reference images. Determine the action, frame count, grid, playback FPS and loop requirement. Default to a simple 8-frame loop (4 columns, 2 rows), 8 FPS. If the user supplies separate frames, use their explicit order and skip generation and splitting. Clarify ambiguous versions, do not request re-upload of existing images.

## Outputs
A GIF animation, ordered PNG frames and an in-app playback preview. No video or audio. GIF has limited colors and binary transparency; retain PNG frames for fidelity.

## Steps
Plan consecutive phases of one action with a fixed camera, identical scale, canvas and baseline. Describe consistent character identity, lighting and background. For loops plan a seamless last-to-first transition without a duplicated endpoint.
Generate ONE equal-cell grid sheet with create_images, output_mode=compose, count=1 and relevant references. Ask for row-major frames, no gaps, borders, labels or overlap between cells. Generation is approximate, not a guarantee of exact grid geometry or motion consistency.
Use view_image to inspect the sheet. Call split_sprite_sheet with its image ID, exact rows, columns, frame_count and margin/spacing (default zero). Use the returned ordered frameFiles with compose_animation, fps and looped. If the grid cannot be divided evenly or the image is misaligned, explain and ask before regenerating; do not keep guessing crop parameters. Tools enforce their own size/frame limits.

## Acceptance
Offer animation playback and PNG frame export for user inspection. State that encoded success alone does not verify smoothness or seamless looping. Report any visible scale shifts, clipping, inconsistent identity or grid problems. Let the user judge actual motion. Never claim to have watched the animation from only a still image.

## Limits
No automatic interpolation, background removal, character alignment or video generation. Additional paid regeneration requires user approval. Keep originals and completed results. Local cutting/encoding does not consume the image-generation count budget.
